run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-16T18:15:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The evidence in this window explains the RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/fraud-detection as a ~2% span error ratio whose error spans are exclusively fraud-detection's flagd flag-evaluation streaming calls. In Jaeger, every error-tagged fraud-detection span is operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with status error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), duration 594-602 s; the corresponding flagd server spans in the same traces carry rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and the exact description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" (532-553 s). The identical EventStream error pattern is present for ad and recommendation, so the shared flagd dependency is implicated rather than fraud-detection's own pods: all 10 fraud-detection pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no last termination, flagd's own container uses 0.0075-0.0093 CPU cores with 0% CPU throttling, and all 12 fault-injection flags in flagd-config have defaultVariant "off". Because all 12 flags are off, a flag-enabled application failure in another service is ruled out as the source. Caveats: Prometheus span-metric samples stop at ~17:45:22 and Jaeger traces at ~17:39, so the 18:15:22 alert evaluation and the exact 0.0222 value are not directly observable, and the RequestErrorRate rule expression could not be read; a ~532-604 s stream lifetime recurring identically across three independent flagd clients also leaves open that these are periodic flag-sync stream re-establishments that trip an "above 0" threshold rather than an acute service failure.

claims.text: fraud-detection is a valid service_name in traces_span_metrics_calls_total; its spans in this window are the consumer operations "orders receive" and "orders process" plus client operations flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt and "resolve".

Among the 65 metric names returned for namespace otel-demo, the only application request/error telemetry is traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket; no rpc_* or http_server_* request metric series appeared.

10 error-tagged fraud-detection spans were returned by Jaeger, all of operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, all with status error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, with durations between 594,101,234 us and 601,796,702 us (about 594-602 s).

The flagd server spans that are children of fraud-detection's failing EventStream client spans are themselves error spans (rpc.grpc.status_code=4) whose otel.status_description reads exactly "stream closed due to server-side timeout"; durations 532,498,814-553,397,947 us.

The same EventStream failure is not unique to fraud-detection: ad's client span flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream also appears with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and durations 598,397,546-604,202,243 us in the same flagd error search.
EventStream STATUS_CODE_ERROR counters rose for three independent flagd clients between 17:35:22 and 17:45:22: ad 5 to 8, fraud-detection 1 to 10 (then 4), recommendation 1 to 7.

Raw fraud-detection counters show flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream STATUS_CODE_ERROR moving 1 to 10 at 17:35:22 and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt STATUS_CODE_ERROR moving 1 to 2, while orders process/orders receive carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no error status) and rise to 230/221.

All 10 fraud-detection pods are phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0 and an empty lastState; the flagd pod is also Running/Ready with 0 restarts for both the flagd and flagd-ui containers.
The fraud-detection Deployment is at revision 1, created 2026-11-16T17:19:22Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-fraud-detection, with readyReplicas 10 of 10 and availableReplicas 10.

The flagd Deployment is the only workload at revision 2 and has two ReplicaSets: flagd-c47676d99 created 17:19:23Z with 0 replicas, and flagd-58db7486bd created 17:21:16Z with 1 ready replica, i.e. the flagd pods were replaced at about 17:21:16Z.

The flagd container runs /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json with no liveness, readiness or startup probe, limits cpu 250m / memory 512Mi, and it consumes 0.0075-0.0093 CPU cores with a 0 CPU-throttling ratio and a 32.8-34.3 MB working set (pod total 202.8-204.3 MB, of which flagd-ui is 169.5 MB).

All 12 flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) are ENABLED with defaultVariant "off": adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodhomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure.

The fraud-detection container is configured with FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 and KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, and has CPU limit 100m; its pods ran at 0.011-0.042 CPU cores with a CPU-throttling ratio of about 0.03-0.23 across pods.

Two kafka pods show container restarts with an Error termination: kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w restartCount 3 with lastState reason Error, exitCode 1, finishedAt 2026-11-16T17:30:45Z, and kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr restartCount 1 with reason Error, exitCode 1, finishedAt 2026-11-16T17:25:48Z.

Cluster events in the window include HPA FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas for kafka, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping and valkey-cart at 17:34-17:34:55Z, FailedGetScale for postgres (count 61), and recommendation HPA scale-down 10 to 8 at 17:35:16Z and 8 to 7 at 17:36:16Z with pods deleted (Killing/SuccessfulDelete at 17:35:16Z and 17:36:16Z).

The single checkout error trace in the window (17:35:17Z) fails with grpc code 13 and otel.status_description "shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post \"http://shipping:8080/get-quote\": EOF", and contains no fraud-detection span.

Data availability ends early relative to the 18:28:30 window end: fraud-detection's span-metric series returned points only through 17:45:22 (the all-service error-rate series likewise end at 17:45:22), Jaeger's fraud-detection traces cover 17:34:18.895468-17:36:35.401890, and frontend traces end at 17:39:43.442572.

Most likely explanation of the 0.0222 RequestErrorRate: the numerator is fraud-detection span errors, and in the observed data those errors are entirely its flagd EventStream client calls that end with gRPC code 4 after flagd closes the stream with a server-side timeout, so the error ratio is produced by the flagd flag-evaluation streaming dependency rather than by fraud-detection's order processing.

Alternative explanation that remains open: the failing EventStream spans all last a very consistent ~532-604 s (about 9-10 minutes) and the same behaviour appears simultaneously on three independent flagd clients (ad, fraud-detection, recommendation), which is consistent with periodic re-establishment of the long-lived flag-sync stream rather than one acute outage; an alert that fires when the error ratio is merely above 0 would then be reporting routine streaming churn.

Against flagd being crashed or resource-starved: flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, the flagd container's CPU is 0.0075-0.0093 cores against a 250m limit with 0 CPU-throttling ratio, and its working set is 32.8-34.3 MB against a 512Mi limit and a 60MiB GOMEMLIMIT.

Against a fault-flag-driven application failure (paymentFailure, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, etc.) being the source: every flag in flagd-config currently has defaultVariant "off".

Against fraud-detection itself being broken: all 10 replicas are Ready with 0 restarts and no last termination state, the Deployment is at revision 1 with no recent rollout (created 17:19:22Z), and no error status was observed on its orders receive/orders process spans.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the kafka pod restarts with exitCode 1 (kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w 3 restarts finishing 17:30:45Z, kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr 1 restart finishing 17:25:48Z). They are real changes in the window, but no error status appears on fraud-detection's consumer spans and all of its error-tagged spans are flagd calls, so there is no evidence tying the restarts to this error rate.

Rejected as evidence about fraud-detection: the checkout/frontend 500 error at 17:35:17Z is a shipping dependency failure ("shipping quote failure: failed POST to shipping service: Post http://shipping:8080/get-quote: EOF", grpc code 13); its trace contains no fraud-detection span.

Rejected as the main driver: CPU throttling of fraud-detection pods (about 0.03-0.23 of CFS periods, worst pod 0.229) is not supported as the cause, because the flagd server span itself reports the stream closing due to a server-side timeout and flagd's own throttling ratio is 0.

Read the RequestErrorRate rule expression and threshold; if it is errors/total spans with a threshold above 0, any single flag-sync stream error trips it - consider excluding long-lived flagd EventStream/streaming spans from the numerator or using a non-zero threshold.

Ask the flagd owners whether a ~532-604 s EventStream lifetime ending in a server-side timeout is expected for flagd v0.12.8 as configured on Deployment flagd; if not, review that Deployment (revision 2, rolled at ~17:21:16Z) and its stream/keepalive settings, and restore sampled metrics/traces past 17:45 so the 18:15:22 evaluation can be verified.

gaps: No Prometheus span-metric samples exist after about 17:45:22 and no Jaeger traces after about 17:39, so the alert's evaluation at 18:15:22 and the reported current value 0.0222 could not be observed directly; whether the error rate persisted, grew or recovered by 18:15 is unknown.

The RequestErrorRate rule expression and threshold could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and unfiltered, so it is unknown whether the alert counts spans or requests and over which window.

No application logs were available for fraud-detection: both containers of fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l returned 0 lines in the window and no previous container instance existed; flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx likewise returned 0 lines per container.

The change_history integration is not available, so what changed in the flagd Deployment rollout at ~17:21:16Z (revision 1 to revision 2, new ReplicaSet flagd-58db7486bd) and whether flagd-config was modified could not be determined; all workloads were created at 17:19:22Z, so there is no earlier baseline to judge whether ~2.2% error ratio is abnormal for fraud-detection.

Prometheus scrape-target health could not be checked: get_prometheus_target for job otel-collector returned active_targets_total 0 with an empty jobs_seen list, and up{job="otel-collector"} returned no series.

The 2 flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt error spans counted in the metric could not be retrieved from Jaeger (no trace matched that operation with error=true), so their gRPC status code and error description are unknown.
The kafka pod restarts with exitCode 1 (17:25:48Z and 17:30:45Z) are unexplained and are not placed as affected by or as a cause of this alert.

No span named with "Fraud" is present in span metrics, so synchronous caller-side impact on fraud-detection could not be measured; the query returned no data rather than proving that no such caller exists.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule (expression, window, threshold) and evaluate it against the flagd EventStream span series to confirm the 0.0222 numerator/denominator.

Confirm with the flagd maintainers whether a ~10-minute EventStream lifetime ending with "stream closed due to server-side timeout" is expected behaviour, and if not, review the flagd Deployment revision 2 configuration from ~17:21:16Z.
Extend the telemetry window past 17:45 (Prometheus span metrics) and past 17:39 (Jaeger) so the 18:15:22 alert evaluation can be verified and the persistence of the error rate measured.
Separately review the kafka pod restarts ending in exitCode 1 at 17:25:48Z and 17:30:45Z, which are not explained by this evidence and are not tied to the fraud-detection error spans.
